title: Personal Credit Cards: Quantity and Cash Value of a Closing Cash-Out
content:
This page fixes how many Personal Credit Cards points a closing cash-out takes and what it pays.

## Rule

- The cash-out takes every point still remaining on the card, in a single deposit into the receiving account.
- Nothing is cashed out when the remaining points fall below the tier's smallest redemption.
- Nothing is cashed out when there is no receiving account for the cash-out.
- The cash paid equals the points cashed out times the tier's per-point cash worth, taken to the nearest cent with halves going up. The tier's travel worth per point never applies to a deposit.

## Truth table

| Remaining points reach the smallest redemption | A receiving account exists | Points cashed out |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | all remaining points |
| yes | no | none |
| no | yes | none |
| no | no | none |

## Worked cases (hypothetical; a smallest redemption of 3000 points is assumed only for illustration)

- A card with 12205 remaining points and a receiving account: all 12205 points are cashed out in one deposit.
- A card with 2750 remaining points: nothing is cashed out.
